You are the proposer in an automated research loop on a GPU rental price forecaster. Each target is a published daily
median of provider offers (USD per GPU-hour) from public collectors; the forecaster gives q10, q50 and q90 at 1, 3 and 7 days.
Loss is pinball loss averaged over the three quantiles; skill = 1 - loss / loss of the last value (flat forecast, zero width);
pooled skill sums losses over cells. You change the system only through one rule in the grammar below, and a fixed test decides.

CURRENT SYSTEM
Base: equal-weight blend (mean of log quantiles) of the members available in each cell: mix, gbm, chronos, analog, prov, fm2, fragility.
Members: mix = pooled empirical change quantiles conditioned on the series' recent-change state; gbm = gradient-boosted quantile regression on series features; chronos = pretrained time-series model (Chronos-Bolt-small, long context, centre = last value); analog = nearest-neighbour analog windows across series; prov = simulation of the provider offers behind the published median; fm2 = pretrained time-series model with 16 days of context, centre = last value; fragility = mix with tails moved to the one-offer-out and one-offer-in medians of the panel; drift = the organisers' baseline: last value times empirical quantiles of the series' own h-day log changes (not in the base blend).

RULE GRAMMAR
A candidate rule is a JSON object {"when": CONDITION, "do": ACTION}.
CONDITION is one of:
  {"fact": NAME, "op": OP, "value": V}   numeric facts: op < <= > >= == != with a number; a missing value makes every comparison false
                                        boolean facts: op == != with true or false
                                        category facts: op == != with a string, or "in" with a list of strings
  {"all": [CONDITION, ...]}   {"any": [CONDITION, ...]}   {"not": CONDITION}
  at most 6 comparisons and 3 levels of nesting. Only the facts listed above exist; unknown facts, values, members or actions are errors.
ACTION is one of (applied to the current system's forecast in the cells where the condition holds; rules apply in order, the new rule last):
  {"action": "members_only", "members": [MEMBER, ...]}  recompute the blend from only these members (cells where none of them gives a forecast keep the current forecast)
  {"action": "drop_members", "members": [MEMBER, ...]}  recompute the blend without these members (from the members currently in the cell's blend)
  {"action": "add_drift"}  add drift as a member of the cell's blend and recompute it
  {"action": "last_zero"}  replace the forecast by the last value with zero width (q10 = q50 = q90 = last)
  {"action": "scale_width", "lo": number in [0.0, 3.0], "hi": number in [0.0, 3.0]}  multiply the log distance of q10 below q50 by lo and of q90 above q50 by hi (0..3; 1 = unchanged)
  {"action": "centre_last"}  move the whole forecast so q50 equals the last value, keeping its log distances
  {"action": "cover_last"}  widen the interval just enough to contain the last value (q10 = min(q10, last), q90 = max(q90, last))
  {"action": "shrink_to_last", "w": number in [0.0, 1.0]}  move every quantile toward the last value in log: q = exp((1 - w) log q + w log last), w in 0..1
MEMBER is one of: mix, gbm, chronos, analog, prov, fm2, fragility, drift.
Format example only (it selects no cell and changes nothing): {"when": {"all": [{"fact": "horizon", "op": "==", "value": 3}, {"fact": "rows", "op": "<", "value": 0}]}, "do": {"action": "scale_width", "lo": 1.0, "hi": 1.0}}

STEP 1 OF 2. Before proposing a rule you may ask for up to three further breakdowns of the selection data, each by one or two facts
(numeric facts are cut at their quartiles; "cause" is also allowed), optionally restricted by a condition in the grammar above.
Also write one web search query for prior work on the mechanism you suspect (it searches sources published on or before 2026-09-18).
Reply with JSON only: {"breakdowns": [{"by": ["FACT"], "where": null}], "search_query": "...", "focus": "one sentence on what you will look at"}
